description:
Found while triaging fz-kdt.130's crash trio; SEPARATE root from .130 and
still live after .130's fix. Interp door only -- JIT and AOT are correct.

Witness:

    fn main() do
      send(self(), {:job, fn (n) -> n + 1 end})
      receive do
        {:job, f} -> dbg(f.(41))
      end
    end

  fz2 interp -> panic "RefCell already borrowed" at runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:200
  fz2 run    -> 42 (correct)
  fz2 build  -> 42 (correct)

Backtrace (the whole mechanism):

    <fz_runtime::heap::Heap>::alloc_closure_slots        <- schemas.borrow_mut()
    deep_copy::deep_copy_strict_closure
    deep_copy::deep_copy_any_value
    deep_copy::deep_copy_strict_struct                   <- holds schemas.borrow()
    deep_copy::deep_copy_any_value
    deep_copy::deep_copy_tagged_bits
    deep_copy::deep_copy_any_value_ref
    <fz::ir_interp::IrInterpRuntime>::send_opaque

`deep_copy_strict_struct` reads the struct's schema through
`Heap::schemas.borrow()` and keeps that borrow live while it recurses into the
struct's fields. A closure field then needs `Heap::closure_schema_id`, which
takes `schemas.borrow_mut()` on the same `RefCell` -- re-entrant borrow, panic.

Not a closure/mailbox-typing problem: it is the copy walk holding a registry
borrow across recursion. A closure inside a LIST message copies fine (cons
cells, no schema read), which is why the corpus never hit it.

Fix shape: the schema read and the recursion must not overlap -- take what the
walk needs from the registry, drop the borrow, then recurse. Worth checking
every deep_copy_strict_* arm for the same overlap, not just the struct one.
title: P1: interp send deep-copy re-enters the schema registry when a closure sits inside a struct message
